test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Mechanic Diesel) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following components in the axle is the most likely to fail if there is an unusual loud clanking or clunking as you put your vehicle into gear, or if a vehicle seems to struggle to get power as it starts to move?

options.text: There is a crack initiated in the axle at cross sectional area perpendicular to axis
Bearing at the wheel is damaged

solution:
The correct answer is __Axle-joint damage**(Option 1)**.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• Axle-joint damage__ is a common cause of loud clanking or clunking sounds when the vehicle is put into gear.
 
• This damage can impair the transfer of power from the transmission to the wheels.
 
• Axle joints, such as universal joints or CV joints, are crucial for proper functioning and smooth movement of the axle.
 
• When these joints are damaged, the vehicle may struggle to move or exhibit unusual sounds during operation.
 
• Regular maintenance and inspection can prevent axle-joint damage and ensure efficient vehicle performance.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Crack in the axle:**

 
 
• A crack in the axle can lead to structural failure, but it is less likely to cause clanking or clunking sounds immediately.
 
• Cracks often develop gradually and may require professional inspection to identify.
 
 
 
• **Bearing at the wheel:**
 
 
• Wheel bearing damage usually causes grinding or humming noise rather than clanking or clunking sounds.
 
• It affects wheel rotation and can lead to uneven tire wear or vibration.
 
 
 
• **Bending in the shaft:**
 
 
• A bent shaft may lead to vibrations or misalignment, but it does not typically cause loud clanking sounds.
 
• Such issues are often identified during vehicle inspections.
